context: The available denominations are 1, 2, and 5 yuan (3 types, each reusable). The target is 4 yuan. State dp[i, a] is the minimum coin count to make amount a exactly using the first i denominations. The two-dimensional dp table has 4 rows (i from 0 to 3) and 5 columns (a from 0 to 4).

MAX = target amount + 1 = 5 marks an unreachable state (no solution). It is not a count of 5 coins. Amount 0 needs no coins, so the first column has boundary value 0. With no denominations (i = 0), every positive amount is unreachable.
description: Create a 4×5 zero table. Set the first-row positive amounts dp[0, 1] through dp[0, 4] to the unreachable marker MAX = 5. Keep the first column dp[0, 0] through dp[3, 0] at the valid boundary value 0. Fill rows i = 1 through 3, visiting a = 1 through 4 in each. If the denomination exceeds a, skip it and copy dp[i - 1, a] from above. Otherwise, compare dp[i - 1, a] above (skip) with dp[i, a - denomination] + 1 from the left in this row (take one coin) and choose the smaller count. Reading the current row allows reuse of the same denomination.

Each step includes a complete dp table named for its step and action. Row headers give i and the available denominations, and column headers give the amount. The first column is labeled “boundary set,” and unreachable first-row cells are labeled “MAX, unreachable boundary.” Earlier results are “computed.” An “uncomputed initial value” is a placeholder, not a minimum count. A newly calculated cell is labeled “written this step.” The final step labels the bottom-right cell “return value.” The step 15 table contains all final values.

frames.announcement: Create the initial 4×5 dp table of zeros, ready to set the first-row unreachable boundary to MAX.
frames.explanation: For 3 denominations (1, 2, 5) and target 4, create a 4×5 dp table (rows i = 0–3, columns a = 0–4). All entries initially default to 0. In the first column, 0 is already the correct boundary: zero coins make 0 yuan. Zeros at positive amounts are uncomputed placeholders. The first-row unreachable boundary will be set to MAX next.
frames.key_state: Initial 4×5 zero table: the first column has boundary value 0. Positive amounts hold initial placeholders of 0 until the first-row MAX boundary is set.

frames.title: Create an initial 4×5 dp table of zeros

frames.announcement: Set positive amounts in the first row to the unreachable marker MAX = 5. Keep the first column at its boundary value of 0.
frames.explanation: With no coins (i = 0), no positive amount can be made. Set dp[0, 1] through dp[0, 4] in the first row to MAX = 5, meaning no solution, not a count of 5. Amount a = 0 needs zero coins, so dp[0, 0] through dp[3, 0] in the first column keep their boundary value 0. Zeros for positive amounts in rows 1–3 are still uncomputed placeholders.
frames.key_state: Boundaries set: dp[0, 1] through dp[0, 4] in the first row equal MAX (5, unreachable). The first column is 0. The 12 interior cells await calculation.

frames.title: Set positive amounts in the first row to the unreachable boundary MAX = 5

frames.announcement: Calculate dp[1, 1] (denomination 1, amount 1): add 1 to dp[1, 0] in this row to get 1 coin.
frames.explanation: For the first denomination (1), calculate dp[1, 1] at a = 1. Skipping this coin gives dp[0, 1] = MAX (5, unreachable) from above. Taking a 1-yuan coin adds 1 to the boundary dp[1, 0] = 0 on the left in this row, giving 1. Write min(MAX, 1) = 1 to dp[1, 1]. This uses 1 one-yuan coin.
frames.key_state: dp[1, 1] (denomination 1, amount 1): min(MAX, dp[1, 0] + 1) = 1, a minimum of 1 coin.

frames.explanation: For the first denomination (1), calculate dp[1, 2] at a = 2. Skipping this coin gives dp[0, 2] = MAX (unreachable) from above. Taking a 1-yuan coin adds 1 to the value dp[1, 1] = 1 on the left in this row, giving 2. Write min(MAX, 2) = 2 to dp[1, 2]. This uses 2 one-yuan coins.
frames.key_state: dp[1, 2] (denomination 1, amount 2): min(MAX, dp[1, 1] + 1) = 2, a minimum of 2 coins.

frames.key_state: dp[1, 3] (denomination 1, amount 3): min(MAX, dp[1, 2] + 1) = 3, a minimum of 3 coins.

Taking a 1-yuan coin adds 1 to the value dp[1, 3] = 3 on the left in this row, giving 4. Write min(MAX, 4) = 4 to dp[1, 4]. This uses 4 one-yuan coins. This completes row 1.
frames.key_state: dp[1, 4] (denomination 1, amount 4): min(MAX, dp[1, 3] + 1) = 4, a minimum of 4 coins. This completes row 1.

frames.announcement: Calculate dp[2, 2] (denomination 2, amount 2): one 2-yuan coin uses fewer coins than the two needed if we skip it. Write 1.
frames.explanation: For denomination 2 and amount a = 2, skipping the coin gives dp[1, 2] = 2 from above (two 1-yuan coins). Taking one adds 1 to the boundary dp[2, 0] = 0 on the left in this row, giving 1 (one 2-yuan coin). Write min(2, 1) = 1 to dp[2, 2].
frames.key_state: dp[2, 2] (denomination 2, amount 2): min(2, dp[2, 0] + 1) = 1, one 2-yuan coin.

frames.announcement: Calculate dp[2, 3] (denomination 2, amount 3): add one 2-yuan coin to dp[2, 1] = 1 and write the minimum count of 2.
frames.explanation: For denomination 2 and amount a = 3, skipping the coin gives dp[1, 3] = 3 from above (three 1-yuan coins). Taking one adds 1 to dp[2, 1] = 1 on the left in this row (one 1-yuan coin), giving 2 coins, one of each. Write min(3, 2) = 2 to dp[2, 3].
frames.key_state: dp[2, 3] (denomination 2, amount 3): min(3, dp[2, 1] + 1) = 2, one 1-yuan coin and one 2-yuan coin.

frames.announcement: Calculate dp[2, 4] (denomination 2, amount 4): reuse dp[2, 2] = 1 in this row and add one more 2-yuan coin. Write 2 coins.
frames.explanation: For denomination 2 and amount a = 4, skipping the coin gives dp[1, 4] = 4 above (four 1-yuan coins). Taking it uses the updated dp[2, 2] = 1 on the left in this row, already containing one 2-yuan coin. Adding another gives 2 coins of 2 yuan. Write min(4, 2) = 2 to dp[2, 4] to finish row 2. Reading from the left in this row permits repeated use of the same denomination.
frames.key_state: dp[2, 4] (denomination 2, amount 4): reuse dp[2, 2] + 1 = 2 in this row (two 2-yuan coins), completing row 2.

frames.explanation: When all transitions are complete, read the highlighted bottom-right cell dp[3, 4] = 2. It differs from MAX (5), so return 2 as the minimum number of coins to make exactly 4 yuan: two 2-yuan coins. A result of MAX would return -1. No values change in this step.
frames.key_state: The table is complete: the bottom-right cell dp[3, 4] = 2 (two 2-yuan coins). It differs from MAX, so return 2.

result: Denomination 5 exceeds every positive amount in the table (1–4), so row 3 copies the results for the first two denominations. If the final value equals MAX, the code returns -1 for no solution.
summary: Fill the table by denomination and target amount to find the fewest coins that make exactly 4 yuan.
